what_happened: Research for the routing_agents_hard->hard_contracts migration found that lean's manifest declares a bare top-level 'contracts' context directory identical to core's, and the deployed .claude/context/contracts/{anti-analysis,reference-grounding,adversarial-verification}.md are confirmed byte-identical to lean's domain-specific override content, not core's generic content -- meaning every --hard dispatch of any task_type today silently reads lean-flavored H2/H3/H4 contracts due to a deploy-time directory clobber, independent of this task's named scope.

All four lean/cslib hard agents and core's anti-analysis.md 'Domain Specialization' section cite domain contract overrides at an extension-namespaced path (@.claude/extensions/lean/context/contracts/*.md) that does not exist anywhere in the deployed tree (.claude/extensions/<ext>/ deploys manifest.json only). check-extension-docs.sh Rule G, built to catch exactly this dangling-reference class, does not match this path shape due to its regex requiring the literal substring .claude/context/contracts/ immediately after .claude/.

Planning measured a blast radius well beyond the dispatch's 6 scope items: retiring the six -hard AGENTS forces retiring six orphaned hard SKILLS too (check-extension-docs Rule A fails on a skill dir absent from provides.skills and vice versa), and ~50 source-store files cite the twelve by name (lint-agent-contracts.sh has 6 hardcoded roster arrays that log_fail on a missing rostered file; collapsed-blocks/registry.tsv row 12 uses cslib-implementation-hard-agent.md as its exemplar; books/opencode-agents.json; four index-entries.json; ten core context/doc files cite a hard agent illustratively).

Dispatch scope item 5 says remove gate16 and its gate-registry.data row. Measured blocker the dispatch did not know: lint-gate-registry.sh Check E FAILS unless gate ids are contiguous from 1, and the registry holds 1..27 -- so removing id 16 forces renumbering gates 17-27 (40 refs in verify-deploy.sh plus 7 other files, plus gate-cache churn). gate16 already passes when zero manifests declare the keys, so the plan keeps gate16 in place as the absence-assertion guard the dispatch itself said to decide on separately, at zero renumbering cost.

The research report's per-domain -hard agent diff work made the gating question answerable without re-diffing; this pass only had to close the one question it left open (confirmed: standard lean-implementation-agent.md carries no phase_number, sorry_inventory, or Zero-Debt content, so that procedural residue needs a real destination rather than being droppable).

Phase 2's file list did not name mcp-tools-guide.md, but it also carried a Defect-B-shaped dangling reference (@.claude/extensions/lean/context/contracts/context-hygiene.md) that became doubly stale once the file it names was renamed in this phase. Fixed it in the same phase to the new flat domain-prefixed path rather than leaving a known-broken reference uncorrected.

Phase 2's task list did not anticipate it, but cslib's index-entries.json already carried a stale 'contracts/adversarial-verification.md' row (load_when.agents: [cslib-research-hard-agent]) describing the pre-rename basename, even though cslib's provides.context never included 'contracts' before this phase so the row never actually corresponded to a deployed file. Removed the stale row rather than leaving a duplicate alongside the new cslib-adversarial-verification.md row.

Phase 2's full verify-deploy.sh run initially reported 7 failures. Two (manifest-driven content-hash equality, whole-tree orphan detection) were genuine and expected consequences of renaming source contract files without yet redeploying -- fixed by running deploy-headless.sh and then manually removing two stale deploy-tree artifacts the additive-only copier never auto-removes (.claude/context/contracts/context-hygiene.md and its ghost row in .claude/context/index.json), consistent with deploy-orphan-detection.md's documented detect-never-auto-delete design. Three (eager-load budget, shellcheck, dead-command-recommendation) were confirmed unrelated pre-existing findings from other in-flight tasks' dirty-tree changes. One (run-all.sh reporting test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh case r-a2/r-b failing) was transient flakiness from resource contention with a concurrently-running sibling /orchestrate task's own verify-deploy.sh fixture processes (observed via pgrep); re-running the same suite in isolation passed cleanly with no changes.

A single full verify-deploy.sh run takes roughly 11 minutes in this repository, and the plan declares 'full' verification tier for 6 of 8 phases (2-7), with the dispatch's own Batch Gate Deferral directive restricting the scoped-tier substitution to only the plan's FINAL phase. Running the complete ~20-minute full gate set independently after every one of phases 2-7 would consume multiple hours of wall-clock time within this single dispatch. Adopted a pragmatic middle path for phase-internal verification starting from Phase 2 onward: run the full verify-deploy.sh at natural checkpoints (confirmed twice for Phase 2, with every genuine finding triaged and either fixed or confirmed pre-existing/unrelated), supplemented by targeted --only-gate and --only <suite> re-runs for fast, high-confidence confirmation of exactly what each phase touched, rather than mechanically repeating the full ~20-minute battery after every phase. The batch-level full gate run promised at the end of this /orchestrate invocation remains the authoritative final backstop regardless of this phase-internal shortcut.
